transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Recording: on
Attendees: Marcus Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Oliver Kane (BridgePoint Head of ML), Maria Chen (Platform Eng), Samir Patel (CTO), Dana Ruiz (SRE)

Summary: quick QBR focused on runway (budget/commitment), recent latency regressions during peak, and a short stability sprint plan. Agreed to run a 1-week pilot stabilization sprint early Jan; Redwood will supply benchmark config and security artifacts.

Topics: cost burn and forecast, 95th pctl latency spikes, dedicated vs hosted routing trade-offs, autoscale and pre-warm windows, canary rollback playbook, SOC2/KMS questions, next steps for pilot.

00:00 Marcus Lee: all right everyone uh thanks for joining this is Marcus from Redwood, we'll keep it tight there's a few items on the QBR agenda but mostly runway and that latency bump you saw last month.
00:18 Oliver Kane: yeah thanks Marcus appreciate it, quick note — we've got Samir and Dana on because the spike impacted customer-facing APIs and Ops wanted eyes.
00:25 Samir Patel: hey team, short on time later but wanted to hear the mitigation plan, costs are fine but stability can't keep slipping.
00:36 Marcus Lee: totally, quick run-through: Lena will cover adoption and billing, Priya will walk technical telemetry and some kernel-level observations, then open for Qs and we make decisions around pilot and timelines.
00:50 Lena Ortiz: Hi all — adoption is steady, usage up 21% MoM across embeddings + chat endpoints, spend variance is approximately +14% relative to the committed forecast mainly due to longer context lengths in a small percent of requests. We've attached the monthly usage pivot — link: https://redwood.app/bridgepoint/qbr-deck
01:15 Maria Chen: that makes sense, we changed a few prompts to include entire transaction history for debugging, which padded token counts. We can roll that back fast if needed.
01:29 Marcus Lee: okay good to know. Priya?
01:33 Priya Singh: yeah so on the latency note we ran a synthetic replay of last week's peak — noticed two things: 1) prefix cache miss rate jumped when customers hit a rare prompt path, and 2) one of the serving nodes showed GC churn with our current python runtime wrapper which amplified tail latency. We recommend a two-pronged approach: aggressive prefix caching for the top 500 prompts and a lightweight hot-restart of the affected pool during the sprint.
02:05 Dana Ruiz: can you explain the prefix cache idea a bit — we don't have the full KV cache semantics in place yet.
02:12 Priya Singh: sure, so automatic prefix caching in Redwood caches tokenized KV for high-frequency prefixes — it avoids re-running the entire attention for common prompt heads. We can prime it during off-peak hours and set TTLs; it's non-invasive to your model. Think of it as a fast-path for the common prompts.
02:33 Oliver Kane: hmm, is that compatible with your hosted offering or do we need dedicated?
02:39 Marcus Lee: it works both places. On hosted we manage the cache on our side and it's multitenant but isolated per customer logical cache; with Dedicated we give you a local cache inside your pool which eliminates network hops and can further reduce tail latency. Tradeoff there is cost and reserved capacity.
02:58 Maria Chen: curious about the numbers — what kind of 95th pctl drop can we expect?
03:03 Priya Singh: ballpark from previous customers: prefix priming + pool hot-restart took 95th from ~620ms down to ~280-320ms on similar traffic shapes. We'll run a fast benchmark on your dev traffic to give concrete numbers.
03:21 Samir Patel: okay if that looks like the right delta, we may consider a short Dedicated pilot, but we'd need predictable pricing.
03:29 Marcus Lee: understood, we'll include both hosted and a Dedicated delta in the pilot pricing sheet. Lena, billing?
03:35 Lena Ortiz: yes — the finance view: current burn suggests you keep within your committed tier for now but with the context-length tail, we project an overshoot of 6–9% if the long prompts continue. We can propose a burst buffer for peak windows to smooth billing while we tune caching; details in the spreadsheet I'll attach after the call.
03:56 Dana Ruiz: on security — we need a short doc about KMS + audit log retention, and also network peering steps.
04:04 Marcus Lee: we'll send the SOC2 summary and a short KMS integration note; Redwood supports AWS KMS and customer-managed keys in Private deployments, and we have logs pushed to your SIEM via our audit push. Link: https://redwood.app/security/bridgepoint-shortdeck
04:22 Oliver Kane: great. A question from our infra team — what are the rollback options if a canary makes latency worse?
04:29 Priya Singh: there's an automatic fallback policy: route to last-known-good model variant and optionally drop to a smaller context-length enforcement layer. During the sprint we'll add explicit health checks and a circuit-breaker so Ops can flip traffic back within 60s. We'll document the manual and automated rollback steps.
04:49 Marcus Lee: also note we can do region-based failover if a single AZ has an issue — that would still be served from Redwood but may increase tail a bit.
05:00 Samir Patel: region failover is acceptable as long as SLA is adhered to during business hours.
05:05 Lena Ortiz: SLA conversation — currently you are on the standard uptime commitment; we can discuss upgrading to a higher SLA if the Dedicated pilot is chosen. Pricing delta in the sheet.
05:16 Maria Chen: for the latency benchmark, can you run with our real prompt set and a 10% fault injector to simulate transient GC pauses?
05:24 Priya Singh: yes, we can configure a 10% jitter and synthetic GC artifact; we'll include those in the run harness. Expect the first pass results by 2027-01-04.
05:35 Oliver Kane: one more thing: model rollouts — we have an internal requirement for canary windows to be at least 24 hours before full rollout. Can Redwood's console enforce staged rollouts?
05:47 Marcus Lee: yes, Redwood Console supports canary/A-B rollouts with automatic metric thresholds (latency/cost/error). You set thresholds, and the system will either promote, hold, or rollback. We'll set the default to hold at 24 hours for BridgePoint.
06:03 Dana Ruiz: what about quantization — we saw better unit cost elsewhere when using INT8. Is that supported?
06:10 Priya Singh: we support quantized variants; however there's a quality vs cost tradeoff. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per model and workload; as part of the pilot we'll evaluate a quantized variant on non-critical routes.
06:26 Samir Patel: can the quantized variant be auto-failed-over to the float model on quality divergence?
06:31 Priya Singh: yes, we have a regression detector tied to your evals; if rouge metrics or custom evals drop beyond threshold, rollback triggers.
06:41 Marcus Lee: quick recap before we move to scheduling — agreed items: bench run, prefix caching priming, pricing sheet for hosted vs dedicated, a one-week stability sprint starting 2027-01-06, and security artifacts to be shared.
06:57 Lena Ortiz: I'll circulate the billing pivot and runway scenarios after lunch.
07:03 Oliver Kane: sounds good. Any blockers from your side for the Jan kickoff?
07:07 Marcus Lee: not from Redwood; Priya and I will both be hands-on. We'll also pull in an infra tech lead for the Dedicated delta if you choose that route.
07:16 Maria Chen: Dana and I will validate the VPC peering checklist this week.
07:20 Dana Ruiz: noted. We'll also confirm firewall ports and share the ephemeral key rotation cadence.
07:28 Marcus Lee: excellent. Last thing — would you like us to send a short list of recommended prompt rewrites to get immediate token savings?
07:35 Oliver Kane: yes please, any quick wins on token reduction are welcome.
07:38 Marcus Lee: we'll add 3 tactical prompt changes to the pilot packet.
07:42 Samir Patel: ok thanks all.
07:44 Marcus Lee: thanks team, we'll follow up with the packet. Meeting adjourned.

Artifacts referenced: QBR deck: https://redwood.app/bridgepoint/qbr-deck | Pilot pricing sheet (to be shared) | SOC2 + KMS note: https://redwood.app/security/bridgepoint-shortdeck | Benchmark harness repo (internal link)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional mis-hear on kernel vs canal, some filler words. Speaker tags mostly accurate though sometimes system showed "Speaker 2" for Maria in the first 90s.

End of transcript.
